key_insight: By combining photoluminescence imaging, drift-diffusion simulations, and Bayesian inference, the study maps where perovskite solar cells degrade and identifies whether the dominant failure originates at the hole/electron transport interfaces or in the bulk.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical diagnostic tool for improving perovskite device stability and guiding targeted interface passivation during solar-cell manufacturing.
method: Photoluminescence imaging of fully fabricated devices
Drift-diffusion simulations linked to Bayesian inference to infer recombination-parameter maps
Time-lapse tracking of inferred maps during accelerated aging (70 °C, full-spectrum light)
evidence_signal: The abstract reports spatially non-uniform parameter changes during aging, with the largest degradation concentrated in perovskite/transport-layer interface regions, and shows that amino-silane passivation suppresses this effect.
watch_item: The inferred degradation maps depend on model assumptions and imaging-to-simulation alignment, so parameter attribution may be sensitive to calibration quality and experimental conditions.
paper_title: Disentangling the origin of degradation in perovskite solar cells via optical imaging and Bayesian inference
